extracted.intended_audience: readers and scholars of American short fiction; anthology editors and general readers
extracted.subtask_description: Selecting and assembling a century-spanning anthology of American short stories (selections drawn from 1915–1998 Best American Short Stories editions) that represent lasting achievement and influence in the genre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endured the test of time
rubrics_metrics.description: These are the stories that have endured the test of time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection prioritizes stories whose value and resonance have persisted across years/decades; choose works that remain readable, discussable, and influential well after initial publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extraordinary stories / masterworks
rubrics_metrics.description: The Best American Short Stories of the Century brings together the best of the best - fifty-five extraordinary stories that represent a century's worth of unsurpassed accomplishments in this quintessentially American literary genre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor works judged as 'masterworks' — exceptional in craft, form, and execution; the anthology aims for the highest level of artistic accomplishment rather than merely competent or notable pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representativeness across the century
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles selected by John Updike from the 1915 through 1998 editions of The best American short stories series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selections should collectively represent the range and development of the American short story over the stated timeframe (1915–1998), showing historical breadth and important moments/styles across the century.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shaped and defined the landscape of the American short story
rubrics_metrics.description: These are the writers who have shaped and defined the landscape of the American short story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize stories and authors whose work exerted clear influence on the genre's form, themes, or trajectory — those that changed expectations or became reference points for later writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unflinching exploration of the human condition
rubrics_metrics.description: Who have unflinchingly explored all aspects of the human condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select stories that probe human experience frankly and deeply — moral complexity, psychological insight, social observation — rather than superficial or purely decorative tales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timelessness / continuing relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Whose works will continue to speak to us as we enter the next century.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize stories with themes, techniques, and emotional power that remain pertinent and communicative to future readers, not just of their own historical moment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorial prominence in the canon
rubrics_metrics.description: Masterworks by such writers as Ernest Hemingway, William Faulkner, Willa Cather, F. Scott Fitzgerald, William Saroyan, Flannery O'Connor, John Cheever, Eudora Welty, Philip Roth, Joyce Carol Oates, Raymond Carver, Cynthia Ozick, and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion often aligns with authors already recognized as major figures; prominence and established critical reputation are implicit selection factors (examples given to illustrate the sort of authors included).
